newsitem.title: UK: BA passenger capacity up 6.7 pct in June.
newsitem.headline: BA passenger capacity up 6.7 pct in June.

text.p: British Airways Plc said its scheduled passenger load factor for June was 0.7 points above last year's performance and its passenger capacity rose by 6.7 percent.

"The growth in traffic was achieved despite the adverse effects of disruption at Charles de Gaulle airport in Paris and the continuing ban on British registered aircraft operating into Nigeria," said the company in a statement.
Premium traffic growth in the month was 3.9 percent compared against an 8.5 percent growth in the main cabin. Cargo tonne kilometres grew by 8.1 percent on the level achieved a year ago.
The company said the threat of strike action by staff is having an impact on forward bookings.

"The uncertainty and the task of bringing our customers back to us after any disruption and the costs associated with the exceptional contingency measures planned to handle potential industrial action, will depress current year profits," said the company.
BA added that the continued strength of sterling will also exacerbate the pressure on reported yields.
BA said the total number of passengers carried rose 5.3 percent to 3.153 million.
